knobs.name: Logic Hz
knobs.description: Logic ticks per second (fixed timestep).
knobs.docstring: Fixed logic tick rate in Hz (Spec §2).

knobs.name: Starting Cash
knobs.description: Cash a fresh founder starts with (intentionally $0).
knobs.docstring: Starting cash for a fresh run. Intentionally $0 (Tim's call): the player taps the "clock in" wage button to earn the cash for their first property, even though that doesn't track thematically. The full origin flow arrives in M2.

knobs.name: Band Step
knobs.description: How much steeper the cost curve gets at each milestone band.
knobs.docstring: Global band-steepening factor; ratio multiplies by this at each milestone band.

knobs.name: Cycle Floor
knobs.description: Fastest a cycle can become from milestone speed-ups (seconds).
knobs.docstring: Minimum cycle length a property can reach via milestone speed-ups, in seconds.

knobs.name: Rush Percent
knobs.description: Cycle fraction one rush-tap advances.
knobs.docstring: Fraction of cycle_length that one rush-tap advances the cycle.

knobs.name: Hold Rush Per Second
knobs.description: Auto-rush pulses per second while holding a property.
knobs.docstring: Auto-rush pulses per second while the rush button is held down.

knobs.name: Wage Hold Taps Per Second
knobs.description: Auto wage-taps per second while holding Clock In.
knobs.docstring: Auto-tap pulses per second while the wage ("clock in") button is held down. This is the BASE rate; the effective rate is meant to be scaled by Legacy upgrades later (configurable by upgrades — GDD §8.4 loophole/upgrade catalog).

knobs.name: Wage Passive Fraction
knobs.description: Seconds of passive income one Clock In tap pays (the executive-pay floor).
knobs.docstring: The "executive compensation" wage floor: one clock-in tap pays at least this many SECONDS of the empire's passive income, whenever that beats the ladder wage (see WageState). Keeps clocking in a viable active play at every scale of the economy; without it the fixed ladder died the moment the first ATM was staffed (Tim, 2026-07-05). At 0.25 and a deliberate ~3 taps/sec, active clocking adds ~+75% on top of passive income.

knobs.name: Wage Floor Bonus Per Level
knobs.description: Executive-pay bonus per clock-in level (0.15 = +15% of the floor per level).
knobs.docstring: Executive-pay bonus per clock-in level, as a fraction of the floor (0.15 = +15%/level). Scales the executive floor by (1 + this × level) so a level-up ALWAYS visibly raises the per-tap payout — without it, once the floor overtook the ladder wage, leveling up changed nothing and the ladder felt dead (Tim, 2026-07-15). A steady multiplier of the floor, so it tracks the economy rather than compounding past it. Tripled from the first-cut 0.05 (Tim, 2026-07-15: clock-in should be more powerful).

knobs.name: Frenzy Fill Hold Factor
knobs.description: Frenzy charge from a held-rush pulse vs a real tap.
knobs.docstring: Frenzy fill per held-rush pulse, as a fraction of a manual tap's fill. Holding is convenient, so it charges the meter slower than real tapping.

knobs.name: Buy Hold Initial Delay
knobs.description: Pause before a held Buy button starts repeating (seconds).
knobs.docstring: Seconds a held BUY button waits before its first auto-repeat.

knobs.name: Buy Hold Repeat Interval
knobs.description: Gap between Buy auto-repeats while held (seconds).
knobs.docstring: Seconds between each BUY auto-repeat after the first.

knobs.name: Hire Hold Initial Delay
knobs.description: Pause before a held Hire/Upgrade button starts repeating (seconds).
knobs.docstring: Seconds a held HIRE/UPGRADE button waits before its first auto-repeat.

knobs.name: Hire Hold Repeat Interval
knobs.description: Gap between Hire/Upgrade auto-repeats while held (seconds).
knobs.docstring: Seconds between each HIRE/UPGRADE auto-repeat after the first.

knobs.name: Epoch Flagship Units Required
knobs.description: How many units of an epoch's FLAGSHIP (its most expensive property) you must own before that epoch will advance — the non-dollar half of the advance gate.  WHY THIS EXISTS (Tim, device report 2026-07-30): an epoch used to end the instant the roster was complete, so the flagship — the property the epoch is named for — got almost no playtime. `sim/EpochPhaseStudy.gd` measured the post-roster "stack" phase at 0.3% of an epoch, and showed that no DOLLAR-denominated fix works: end-of-epoch income grows super-exponentially, so a 10x money threshold is crossed in seconds and reshaping the cost ladder does nothing. A UNIT requirement is different in kind because it can only be satisfied AFTER the roster is complete, in the calmer post-unlock growth regime.  DELIBERATE EXCEPTION to the "defaults mirror tuning.tres" convention: the shipped value is 35, but this default stays 1. 1 reproduces the pre-feature behaviour exactly (owning one of each already implies one flagship), so any code path that builds a TuningConfig without the resource degrades to the old gate rather than to a hard 35-unit wall it never asked for. Not drift — if a defaults-vs-tres audit flags this key, this comment is the answer.

knobs.provenance_notes: Device-tuned (35 in tuning.tres vs 1 fallback default). Requires owning flagship units before advance.

knobs.name: Auto Purchase Base Cadence
knobs.description: Seconds between auto-purchase ticks at upgrade level 1 — the slowest the desk ever runs.
knobs.docstring: Seconds between auto-purchase ticks at upgrade level 1 — the slowest the desk ever runs.

knobs.name: Auto Purchase Min Cadence
knobs.description: Floor on the auto-purchase cadence, reached at the top upgrade level. Guards against a cadence that shrinks to zero and turns the mode into a per-frame buyer.
knobs.docstring: Floor on the auto-purchase cadence, reached at the top upgrade level. Guards against a cadence that shrinks to zero and turns the mode into a per-frame buyer.

knobs.name: Auto Purchase Breadth
knobs.description: How many DISTINCT properties one auto-purchase tick buys into (X in the plan). Fixed rather than upgradable: a cohort is only ~14 properties, so breadth saturates almost immediately and stops being worth selling as an upgrade level.
knobs.docstring: How many DISTINCT properties one auto-purchase tick buys into (X in the plan). Fixed rather than upgradable: a cohort is only ~14 properties, so breadth saturates almost immediately and stops being worth selling as an upgrade level.

knobs.name: Staff Cost Fraction
knobs.description: Alien staff hire cost as a fraction of that epoch's whole economy.
knobs.docstring: Alien staff (tier 2+) ENTRY hire cost as a fraction of the TARGET epoch's whole economy (earth_economy_target × that epoch's economy_scale). Anchoring to the epoch economy — not the property's tiny Earth base cost — is what makes alien staff scale with each epoch, so you cannot afford the next epoch's staff the instant you arrive (Tim 2026-06-17). The Earth staffer (tier 1) keeps its small property-scaled cost. RETUNED 2026-06-27 0.001 → 0.01: at 0.001 the cheapest new staffer was ~0.1% of the epoch's whole economy — trivially affordable at contact, which Tim flagged as "too cheap." At 0.01 the cheapest staffer is ~1% of the epoch economy and the full alien roster costs more than one epoch's earnings, so staffing is a prioritized spend, not a one-tap sweep.

knobs.name: Staff Cost Property Growth
knobs.description: How much pricier each higher rung's staff is.
knobs.docstring: Per-property growth of that fraction: cheaper rungs (ATM) get the base fraction, each higher rung multiplies by this, so pricier properties cost proportionally more to staff.

knobs.name: Staff Level Step
knobs.description: Income added per staff level (additive; cumulative ladder).
knobs.docstring: Base income step per staff level, ADDITIVE. Each block's actual per-level step is this × that block's catalog multiplier (PropertyState.staff_small_step), so later blocks' steps are sized to their epoch while Earth's block 1 keeps exactly this value. Additive (not compounding) because 120 compounding levels would explode income. First-pass value — the Phase 3 pacing retune owns the final numbers (Plans/Epoch_Depth_Pass.md §4).

knobs.name: Staff Levels Per Epoch
knobs.description: Staff levels each epoch unlocks (cap = this × epoch).
knobs.docstring: Levels per block — one block per epoch from the property's unlock epoch onward. The hard cap on staff_level is this × the blocks the run has opened for that property; the cap only ever rises, and the ladder is strictly sequential, so levels skipped earlier are always the next (cheap) rung rather than lost.

knobs.name: Staff Level Cost Base
knobs.description: First staff level's cost as a fraction of the hire price.
knobs.docstring: Cost of a block's SECOND level (the first small step after the hire), as a fraction of that block's own anchor (its hire price). Steps start cheap relative to the hire just paid, then climb by staff_level_cost_growth. Cut 0.10 -> 0.07 (Tim, 2026-07-02) so a level's ROI beats buying a unit.

knobs.name: Staff Level Cost Growth
knobs.description: How much each further staff level costs vs the last (per block).
knobs.docstring: Geometric growth of the step cost WITHIN a block: each level costs the previous × this. The climb restarts every block (an un-reset exponent would make a 120-level ladder literally unbuyable), but each block's anchor is ~economy_scale higher than the last, so absolute costs still trend up. Softened 1.6 -> 1.5 (Tim, 2026-07-02).

knobs.name: Retention Base Cost
knobs.description: Legacy to retain the first property's first staff level.
knobs.docstring: Legacy to retain the FIRST ladder level of the FIRST property (the ATM anchor).

knobs.name: Retention Cost Growth
knobs.description: How much each deeper retained level costs vs the last.
knobs.docstring: Per-LEVEL geometric growth of retention cost within a property (was 1.12 — so flat that levels 1-7 all cost 1 Legacy; 1.25 makes each further step a visible commitment).

knobs.name: Retention Property Step
knobs.description: How much pricier each higher property's retention is.
knobs.docstring: Per-PROPERTY geometric step: each higher property multiplies retention cost by this, so protecting a top earner costs like a top earner (ATM ×1, Executive Assets ×1.5^11 ≈ ×87). The missing term the playtest exposed.

knobs.name: Carb Debug Overlay
knobs.description: 1 shows a live per-row readout of the bubble numbers (diagnosis).
knobs.docstring: 1 = show a tiny per-row debug readout of the live carbonation numbers (excitement level, bubble base speed, measured fill speed, commanded sweep). 0 = off.

knobs.name: Carb Autolog
knobs.description: 1 = on boot, run the scripted CarbAutopilot rush scenario (buy a long-cycle property, hold rush 10s, release, observe) while logging every frame's carbonation internals to user://carb_log.csv, then quit. A desktop diagnosis harness — never ship a build with this on.
knobs.docstring: 1 = on boot, run the scripted CarbAutopilot rush scenario (buy a long-cycle property, hold rush 10s, release, observe) while logging every frame's carbonation internals to user://carb_log.csv, then quit. A desktop diagnosis harness — never ship a build with this on.

knobs.name: Carb Tier Idle Px
knobs.description: Bubble speed on a still/full bar (px/s) — the slowest tier.

knobs.name: Carb Tier Flowing Px
knobs.description: Bubble speed on a normally cycling bar / economy bar (px/s).

knobs.name: Carb Tier Rushed Px
knobs.description: Bubble speed while TURBO is burning (px/s).

knobs.name: Carb Tier Frenzy Px
knobs.description: Bubble speed while a property's rush is held (px/s) — the fastest tier.

knobs.name: Carb Tier Ease
knobs.description: Seconds bubble speed eases over on a tier change (0 = instant, no rush ramp).
knobs.docstring: Seconds a bar's bubble speed/agitation eases over when it changes tier. 0 = INSTANT (no accel/ decel ramp when a rush engages/releases — a held rush is constant from press to release, Tim's long-standing "no edge burst" goal). Raise it only if some smoothing is ever wanted.

knobs.name: Offline Efficiency
knobs.description: Offline income rate vs live play (0–1).
knobs.docstring: Offline income efficiency vs. live play (0–1).

knobs.name: Offline Cap Seconds
knobs.description: Longest offline accrual window (seconds; 14400 = 4h).
knobs.docstring: Base offline accrual cap in seconds (4 hours = 14400).

knobs.name: Frenzy Max Multiplier
knobs.description: Peak income multiplier during a frenzy burn.
knobs.docstring: Peak frenzy multiplier (applied to all income during a burn). Synced 4.0 → 5.6 to match tuning.tres (2026-07-31). It had drifted, which mattered more than usual here because frenzy_pop_floor is SOLVED from this value — at the stale 4.0 the "weakest pop is 2×" floor would be 1/3, not 1/4.6. Keep the two in step.

knobs.name: Frenzy Burn Duration
knobs.description: How long a full frenzy burn lasts (seconds).
knobs.docstring: Duration of a full-charge frenzy burn in seconds.

knobs.name: Frenzy Fill Per Tap
knobs.description: Meter fill added per tap (fraction of the full bar).
knobs.docstring: Meter fill added per tap (fraction of full bar, 0–1).

knobs.name: Frenzy Decay Per Second
knobs.description: Meter decay per idle second (fraction of full bar).
knobs.docstring: Meter decay rate per second when idle (fraction of full bar, 0–1).

knobs.name: Frenzy Idle Grace
knobs.description: Idle seconds before the meter begins to decay.
knobs.docstring: Seconds without a tap before decay begins.

knobs.name: Frenzy Pop Floor
knobs.description: Minimum charge needed to trigger a frenzy.
knobs.docstring: Minimum meter charge at which the player can trigger a frenzy pop.  SOLVED, not hand-picked (Tim, 2026-07-31): the floor is set so a NEW player's weakest possible pop is exactly 2×. A pop pays `1 + (frenzy_max_multiplier − 1) × intensity × meter` (FrenzyState.pop), and a fresh dynasty has intensity 1.0, so     floor = 1 / (frenzy_max_multiplier − 1) = 1 / 4.6 = 0.2174 It was 0.15 (a 1.69× worst pop — the floor barely gated anything and cashing in early locked a weak multiplier), briefly 0.30 (2.38×) before landing on the exact-2× solve.  THIS VALUE DEPENDS ON frenzy_max_multiplier. Change that and this stops meaning 2×; re-solve it. Killer Instinct raises intensity above 1.0, so an invested bloodline's worst pop is higher than 2× by design — the floor pins the new player's case only.  The bar's floor marker and its grayscale-until-poppable treatment both read this, so they follow automatically.
knobs.provenance_notes: SOLVED from frenzy_max_multiplier so that a new player's worst pop is exactly 2.0x.

knobs.name: Heat Build /s
knobs.description: How fast heat climbs while rushing (heat/sec; 1.0 heat = the Hot edge).
knobs.docstring: How fast heat climbs while actively rushing, in heat units per second (0.167 ≈ 6 s from cold to the Hot edge — matching the old build feel).

knobs.name: Hot Heat Build /s
knobs.description: Slower climb rate above the Hot edge (heat/sec; sets time-in-danger).
knobs.docstring: How fast heat climbs while rushing ABOVE heat 1.0 (the OVERDRIVE region), in heat units per second. Slower than the base build so the ride through the danger zone is a real decision window: 0.075 stretches the climb from heat 1.0 to the hard ceiling (0.60 units) to ~8 s (Tim 2026-07-15: "at least 5 to 8 seconds in the high heat zone").

knobs.name: Heat Bleed /s
knobs.description: How fast heat cools when NOT rushing (heat/sec).
knobs.docstring: How fast heat bleeds away when NOT rushing, in heat units per second (0.333 ≈ 3 s to fully cool from heat 1.0 — matching the old bleed feel).

knobs.name: Hard Ceiling
knobs.description: Heat that instantly overheats — the bar's fixed end (vent windows are the real test).
knobs.docstring: The FIXED overheat ceiling — the visible end of the bar and the "you ignored everything" backstop (Plans/Overdrive_Vent_Windows.md). Also the heat at which the bonus reaches the vent ladder's current peak. Replaces the retired random ceiling roll: unpredictability now lives in the vent windows' arrival times, never in the shutdown point itself.

knobs.name: Rush Momentum Cruise Bonus
knobs.description: Safe rush bonus while holding WITHOUT overdrive (0.25 = +25%; capped at the Hot-edge bonus).
knobs.docstring: The sustainable "cruise" bonus while holding rush WITHOUT overdrive engaged (0.25 = +25%). Heat clamps at the matching point on the Building region and can never overheat there — the danger zone is opt-in via the OVERDRIVE button (Plans/Rush_Cruise_Control.md). The Cooling Systems Legacy upgrade adds to this, hard-capped at rush_momentum_bonus_at_hot (the old +30%).

knobs.name: Bonus At Hot
knobs.description: Income bonus at the Hot edge, heat 1.0 (0.30 = +30%).
knobs.docstring: Bonus at the Hot edge (heat 1.0 — the top of the Building region, where OVERDRIVE begins), as a fraction of property income. 0.30 keeps the old cap's value — the Building region is exactly the pre-overheat meter. Above heat 1.0 the bonus is ONE continuous lerp from here to the ladder peak at the hard ceiling (the depth-hazard rework retired the Critical band and its kink — Tim 2026-07-18 evening).

knobs.name: Bonus Peak
knobs.description: Income bonus at max possible heat (0.55 = +55%).
knobs.docstring: Bonus at the hard ceiling with NO vents achieved — the ladder's tier-0 peak. Each successful vent adds rush_momentum_vent_bonus_step on top, with NO cap (endless escalation). Only ever held for seconds at a time — the realistic average is the ride/vent duty cycle (~+75% for a skilled venter; see the vent-window block comment below).

knobs.name: Vent Rate At Cruise
knobs.description: Expected vent checks per second while hovering just past the cruise point (0.05 = about one every 20 s); riding deeper raises the rate.
knobs.docstring: Expected vent-event spawns per second when heat sits just past the cruise point — the SHALLOW end of the depth hazard (0.5 ≈ a check every ~2 s hovering there). Each tick rolls lerp(rate_at_cruise, rate_at_ceiling, depth) × delta against the schedule rng, so arrival stays the unpredictable part while the outcome stays player-owned. Raised 0.05 → 0.5 with the approach phase (2026-07-19): every event now includes approach_seconds of check-free riding, and at the old sparse cadence even a sloppy venter out-earned cruise on free ride time alone — denser checks put the risk back. 0.5 → 0.7 with the refractory (2026-07-18 night), which added the same kind of check-free time (see the tune history above).

knobs.name: Vent Rate At Ceiling
knobs.description: Expected vent checks per second at the very top of the bar (1.0 = about one per second) — the frantic end of the deeper-is-more-frequent ramp.
knobs.docstring: Expected spawns per second at the hard ceiling — the DEEP end of the hazard (relentless). Depth is the cadence axis now: riding higher is the player choosing more checks for more pay. Raised 1.0 → 3.0 with the approach phase, 3.0 → 3.4 with the refractory — same reasoning as rate_at_cruise above both times.

knobs.name: Vent Quiet Min
knobs.description: Shortest rolled quiet time after a vent (or engaging overdrive) before the next event can spawn (seconds).
knobs.docstring: VENT REFRACTORY (Tim 2026-07-18 night): the shortest quiet time after a resolved vent (and after first engaging overdrive) before the next event may spawn. Each vent success rolls a delay uniformly in [refractory_min, refractory_max] on the seeded schedule rng; hazard dice AND the telegraph guarantee's force-spawn both hold their fire until it expires. WHY: deep rides sit so close to the force-spawn bound that the next event used to spawn on almost the very tick a vent resolved — a metronome, not a hazard. A small rolled breather makes the spacing read as random again without touching the depth-hazard curve itself. Tick-time rather than OS time, so a pause or scene reload can never eat part of the breather. (This comment used to say the frenzy freeze pauses it "like every other vent clock" — that freeze was REMOVED 2026-07-19; the vent game now runs straight through a burn. See RushMomentumState.gd:323-330.)

knobs.name: Vent Quiet Max
knobs.description: Longest rolled quiet time before the next vent event (seconds) — the gap is rolled fresh each time so spacing feels random.
knobs.docstring: The longest rolled post-vent quiet time (seconds). The success top-off reserves THIS much extra climb room below the force-spawn bound (see RushMomentumState._succeed_vent), so heat climbing through a worst-case refractory can never leave the next event unable to fit before the hard ceiling — the telegraph guarantee survives the added delay by construction.

knobs.name: Vent Approach Sec
knobs.description: How long an incoming vent event takes to travel across the bar to the trigger point (seconds of warning).
knobs.docstring: The APPROACH PHASE (Tim 2026-07-19): the hazard roll SPAWNS a vent event instead of opening its window instantly, and this is the travel time (seconds of tick time) of the incoming event bar from the bar's right edge to the target — the telegraph lead the player watches before the window opens and the gesture clock starts. Frenzy freeze pauses the flight. Shortened 2.0 → 1.2 with the property freeze (Tim 2026-07-19: "2 seconds feels leisurely — I want to see it coming but not feel like I'm waiting for it"). The shorter flight also attacks the sloppy free ride at its root — less riskless telegraph pay bundled with every check — which, together with the freeze, is what let the fail sting drop to zero below.

knobs.name: Vent Window Sec
knobs.description: Seconds to finish the vent gesture once the window telegraphs.
knobs.docstring: Seconds the player has to COMPLETE the gesture once a window telegraphs — the TIER-0 base of the escalating duration (each tier multiplies it by duration_decay).

knobs.name: Vent Window Decay
knobs.description: Window duration multiplier per tier reached (0.92 = 8% less time each tier).
knobs.docstring: Per-tier multiplier on the window duration (escalation axis 2, SPEED). Retuned from the plan's first-cut 0.92: at 0.92 a ×3 window becomes too short for even a brisk clean triple right when triples begin (~tier 6 — a hard cliff, before the escalating gestures' odds ever get to bite); 0.975 keeps deep windows tight but finishable into the teens, so runs end the designed way — a blown beat on an ever-faster, ever-more-complex gesture.

knobs.name: Vent Window Floor
knobs.description: Shortest the escalating window duration can get (seconds).
knobs.docstring: The duration floor (seconds): the escalating window never shrinks below this — a shorter window stops being a skill check and becomes a reflex lottery.

knobs.name: Vent Lift Step Tiers
knobs.description: Tiers between lift escalations (3 = demand 1 lift, then 2 from tier 3, then 3 from tier 6; max 3 lifts).
knobs.docstring: Tiers between lift escalations (escalation axis 3, COMPLEXITY): required lifts = 1 + tier / this (integer division), so 3 = single at tiers 0-2, double from tier 3, triple from tier 6. HARD-CAPPED at 3 lifts in code — a quad-pump is thumb mush (Tim 2026-07-18); past ×3 the cadence and speed axes carry the difficulty alone.

knobs.name: Vent Gap Max
knobs.description: Longest pause allowed between vent gesture beats (seconds; bigger = more forgiving).
knobs.docstring: Max gap between gesture beats — finger-up time before the re-press must land (seconds).

knobs.name: Vent Tap Max
knobs.description: Longest press that still counts as the quick middle tap of VENT x2 (seconds).
knobs.docstring: Max press length that still counts as the ×2 gesture's middle tap (seconds); a longer hold is a fumbled re-hold, which misses the window.

knobs.name: Vent Heat Drop
knobs.description: Heat released by a successful vent (small drop = deep runs keep riding near the top).
knobs.docstring: Heat vented on a successful gesture (floored at the cruise point — success never ends the ride). Retuned 0.15 → 0.06 for the endless model: smaller than the heat built between checks, so the bar CREEPS TOWARD THE CEILING as tiers deepen — deep runs visibly ride just under the backstop (drama AND pay: the overdrive bonus scales with how high the bar sits, and under the depth hazard so does the check cadence). A success additionally clamps heat down just enough that the next window always fits (see RushMomentumState._succeed_vent — the telegraph guarantee's other half).

knobs.name: Vent Bonus Step
knobs.description: Peak bonus added per successful vent (0.20 = +20% per rung; no cap).
knobs.docstring: Bonus added to the ladder's peak per successful vent (0.30 = +30 percentage points), with NO cap — the difficulty curve is the brake, not the reward curve (Tim 2026-07-18). The peak is only ever tasted near the top of a deep ride (a median skilled run tops out around +55% + 8 × 30% = +295% peak, held for seconds; the honest long-session average is the ~+75% the sim measures). Trimmed 0.60 → 0.30 for the approach phase (2026-07-19): every check now carries approach_seconds of paid telegraph riding, so the same tier pays for roughly twice as long — at the old step even a 70%-reliability rider out-earned cruise, killing the risk.

knobs.name: Vent Fail Re-arm /Tier
knobs.description: Extra re-arm seconds per earned vent tier when you overheat; 0 = off.
knobs.docstring: Extra re-arm seconds per achieved vent tier when an excursion overheats — falling from higher hurts more. Applied BEFORE the Rapid Restart lockout scale (which divides the total). ZEROED with the OVERHEAT PROPERTY FREEZE (Tim 2026-07-19). The sting had been ratcheted up (3 → 6 → 12) solely to keep a sloppy rider from out-earning cruise; the freeze now carries that deterrent for real — an overheat takes the rushed property itself offline for the whole lockout, a cost proportional to what was gambled — and the sim's freeze-priced gates actually FORCE the sting down: at the original 3.0/9.0 a skilled venter nets only +45% (below the +62% worth-the-risk floor), and ~1.0/3.0 is the highest sting that still passes. Zero is both the floor the gates allow and Tim's stated direction ("failure pressure from difficulty, not timeouts"); falling from higher STILL hurts more, because a higher fall drains longer and the frozen property is dark for all of it. The knob stays live in Balance Tuning should device feel want a token sting back (keep ≤ ~1.0 s/tier).

knobs.name: Vent Fail Re-arm Cap
knobs.description: Most extra re-arm seconds the per-tier sting can add (keeps deep-run failures from ever-longer timeouts).
knobs.docstring: Cap on the per-tier re-arm sting (seconds). Deep runs must NOT earn ever-longer timeouts — Tim's direction (2026-07-18) is that failure pressure comes from the difficulty curve, not the punishment; past this the fall costs the same no matter how high it was from. Zeroed with the per-tier sting above (the property freeze is the punishment now — see its tune note); the cap machinery stays in code and in the panel for the same what-if reason.

knobs.name: Overheat Drain /s
knobs.description: Heat drained per second while overheated (sets the lockout length).
knobs.docstring: Heat drained per second while OVERHEATED (the locked cooldown). 0.16 ≈ a 10 s lockout from a full 1.6 ceiling; the visibly draining bar is the cooldown display.

knobs.name: Re-arm Seconds
knobs.description: Extra delay after a full cool-down before rushing re-enables.
knobs.docstring: Extra delay (seconds) after an overheated property fully cools before rushing re-enables — the extra sting Tim asked for beyond the drain itself.

knobs.name: Momentum Grace Sec
knobs.description: How long you still count as rushing after your last rush (bridges the pulse gaps).
knobs.docstring: Grace window (seconds): you still count as "rushing" for momentum this long after your last rush. Must exceed the rush pulse interval (1 / hold_rush_per_second = 0.2 s at 5/s) so momentum keeps building smoothly BETWEEN the discrete auto-rush pulses instead of bleeding in the gaps.

knobs.name: Overheat Haptic ms
knobs.description: Vibration length (ms) when a rush overheats; 0 = off.
knobs.docstring: Haptic pulse lengths (milliseconds) for the momentum bar's feedback beats: the long thump on overheating and the tick when rushing re-arms. Live knobs so the haptic device pass can be dialed on the phone without a code round-trip (phones vary a lot in how a given pulse length feels). 0 disables that pulse. (The old Critical band-crossing tap retired with its band — the vent telegraphs are the drama now.)

knobs.name: Ready Haptic ms
knobs.description: Vibration length (ms) when rushing re-arms after a lockout; 0 = off.

knobs.name: Vent Haptic ms
knobs.description: Vibration length (ms) of EACH vent telegraph pulse — one pulse per required lift, so a x2 window buzzes twice; 0 = off.
knobs.docstring: The vent-window telegraph's own pulse — long enough that "act NOW" is distinguishable by feel alone with the eyes on the property row (plan follow-up item). The telegraph fires ONE PULSE PER REQUIRED LIFT (Tim 2026-07-20): a x2 window buzzes twice, a x3 three times, so the thumb learns the demand before the eyes read the pips — deliberate redundant encoding for the moment the mechanic is fastest.

knobs.name: Vent Haptic Gap ms
knobs.description: Silence (ms) between those vent telegraph pulses, so a x2/x3 reads as counted beats instead of one long buzz.
knobs.docstring: Silence between those telegraph pulses (milliseconds). Without a gap a x3 window would feel like one long buzz rather than three counted beats, which is the whole point of the pulse train. 0 runs the pulses back-to-back.

knobs.name: Estate Exemption Base
knobs.description: Estate-tax-free amount at death ($).
knobs.docstring: Base estate-tax exemption in dollars.

knobs.name: Estate Tax Rate Base
knobs.description: Estate tax rate before loopholes (0–1).
knobs.docstring: Base estate tax rate (0–1). Intentionally brutal; loophole tree is the relief.

knobs.name: Loophole Rate Floor
knobs.description: Lowest the estate tax can fall via loopholes.
knobs.docstring: Floor for the estate tax rate after loopholes (can never go below this).

knobs.name: Legacy Payout Scale
knobs.description: Legacy payout scale on the power curve (K × (net/floor) ^ alpha).
knobs.docstring: Coefficient on the Legacy gain curve (see EstateWaterfall.legacy_gain): legacy = floor(K_LEGACY × (estate_net / floor) ^ ALPHA), where the floor is EstateWaterfall.LEGACY_BASE. Raised 0.045 → 0.50 (Tim 2026-07-14) to keep the FIRST prestige near its old ~350 gems after alpha_legacy was lowered to 0.22 — the two move together (a lower exponent needs a higher coefficient to hold the same yield at the founder's estate scale).
knobs.provenance_notes: Prestige retune. Moves inversely with alpha_legacy to anchor first prestige at ~350 gems.

knobs.name: Legacy Payout Curve
knobs.description: Legacy curve exponent; lower = flatter yield, tames the prestige runaway.
knobs.docstring: Exponent on the estate-magnitude term of the Legacy curve — how fast gems grow with earnings. Lowered 0.30 → 0.22 (Tim 2026-07-14) to flatten the prestige runaway (at 0.30 the yield compounded ~18× per epoch, driving income to ×237 over a dynasty); paired with the upgrade-cost nerf below so the correction is split. Still rewards a better run (~+16% gems per 2× estate), just less punchy.
knobs.provenance_notes: Prestige retune (2026-07-23). Exponent on estate net worth for Legacy gem payout.

knobs.name: Legacy Upgrade Cost Multiplier
knobs.description: Global x on every Legacy upgrade cost — the prestige-power brake (higher = a prestige buys fewer levels).
knobs.docstring: Global multiplier on EVERY Legacy upgrade's cost (LegacyUpgradeCatalog.cost_multiplier). 1.0 = the authored prices; >1 makes a prestige's gems buy fewer upgrade levels, the second brake (with the lower alpha_legacy) on the multiplier runaway that made late epochs trivial (Tim 2026-07-14).
knobs.provenance_notes: Prestige retune brake (3.0x on all Legacy upgrade costs).

knobs.name: Legacy Knee Net
knobs.description: Estate net where the mint curve bends to the deep exponent ($).
knobs.docstring: The estate net where the Legacy mint curve BENDS (Plans/Endgame_Economy.md, Tim 2026-07-28): below this the approved alpha_legacy power curve applies exactly; above it the shallow alpha_legacy_deep exponent takes over, so deep-frontier estates (1e80+) mint ~billions instead of septillions — big numbers that still read as valuable.
knobs.inline_comment: feel-tune (~the $1-sextillion estates the curve was tuned on)
knobs.provenance_notes: Piecewise knee ($1e21) where mint curve switches to deep exponent.

knobs.name: Alpha Legacy Deep
knobs.description: Mint exponent ABOVE the knee (0.06 = +15% gems per 10x deeper estate).
knobs.docstring: The mint curve's exponent ABOVE the knee — how fast gems keep growing once estates pass the tuned range. 0.06 = a 10x deeper estate mints ~+15% more gems (Tim: endgame mints should read in the BILLIONS; the old single-exponent curve ran to septillions).
knobs.provenance_notes: FITTED by DynastyArcStudy (0.05 vs Tim's seed 0.06). Keeps endgame frontier mints in billions.

knobs.name: Legacy Cost Steepening
knobs.description: Upgrade cost growth's own per-level multiplier — the uncapped shop's brake.
knobs.docstring: The upgrade shop's cost STEEPENING (LegacyUpgradeCatalog.cost_steepening): each level's cost-growth factor is itself multiplied by this per level, so the curve starts near the authored per-level growth and steepens without limit — the uncapped compounders' real brake (Plans/Endgame_Economy.md "Shape 2", Tim 2026-07-28). 1.0 = the old flat geometric.
knobs.inline_comment: fit: DynastyArcStudy (1.03 seed missed the dozen-run summit)
knobs.provenance_notes: FITTED by DynastyArcStudy (1.10 vs Tim's seed 1.03). Critical brake on uncapped compounders.

knobs.name: Challenge Bonus Scale
knobs.description: Global x on every Challenge tier payout, both tracks (1.0 = authored ~24% income + 24% Legacy across all six games maxed).
knobs.docstring: Global multiplier on every Challenge tier payout, both tracks. 1.0 = the authored schedule (~24/24 across all six games). Raise to make mastery pay more, lower to soften it. Plans/Challenge_Mode.md.

knobs.name: Challenge Timer Start Seconds
knobs.description: Challenge keep-alive run timer's starting seconds — a run begins with this on the clock and drains until scoring tops it up (Wave 2).
knobs.docstring: The Challenge keep-alive run TIMER's starting seconds — a run begins with this little on the clock and drains until scoring tops it up (Wave 2 mechanic; ChallengeGoals reads it). Plans/Challenge_Mode.md.

knobs.name: Challenge Timer Cap Seconds
knobs.description: Challenge keep-alive run timer's max seconds — top-ups never bank the clock past this (Wave 2).
knobs.docstring: The Challenge keep-alive run TIMER's maximum seconds — top-ups never bank the clock past this, so a strong streak can't stockpile a huge cushion (Wave 2 mechanic). Plans/Challenge_Mode.md.

knobs.name: Challenge Miss Penalty Ratio
knobs.description: Fraction of a hit's time-gain a MISS costs the keep-alive timer (0.5 = half): a dropped Catch coin / failed Timing lock drains this x what the hit would have added.
knobs.docstring: Fraction of a hit's time-gain that a MISS costs the keep-alive timer, in challenge minigames (0.5 = half). A dropped Catch coin / a failed Timing lock drains this ratio x what catching/landing it would have added, so missing hurts proportionally to the hit it replaced. Plans/Challenge_Mode.md.

knobs.name: Challenge Show All Games
knobs.description: 1 shows every minigame on the CHALLENGES screen, ignoring which ones you have met (testing aid; display only — it never marks a game as met).
knobs.docstring: 1 = the CHALLENGES screen shows EVERY minigame regardless of which ones the bloodline has met at a transition; 0 = only the met ones (the shipped rule, Roadmap §8). A dev/testing switch: six games are dealt at random, so reaching one specific game otherwise means replaying transitions until it comes up. DISPLAY ONLY — it never writes to the met set, so turning it off restores the real progress. A 0/1 float rather than a bool because the Balance Tuning panel only renders int and float properties (same convention as carb_debug_overlay).

knobs.docstring: Cadence in active seconds between event rolls.

knobs.name: Event Base Chance
knobs.description: Rare Events: base probability on each roll interval (0..1).
knobs.docstring: Base probability of triggering an event on each roll interval.

knobs.name: Event Grace Period Seconds
knobs.description: Rare Events: grace period at generation start before events fire.
knobs.docstring: Grace period in active seconds at the start of a generation before random events can fire.

knobs.name: Earth Economy Target
knobs.description: Total money on Earth; capture it to win ($).
knobs.docstring: Total money in Earth's economy; capturing this wins the planet.

knobs.name: Autosave Cadence
knobs.description: Seconds between autosaves.
knobs.docstring: Autosave interval in seconds.

knobs.name: Audio Tap Scale Reset Seconds
knobs.description: How long a gap in tapping resets the musical tap scale back to its root note, in seconds.
knobs.docstring: How long a gap in tapping resets the musical tap scale back to its root note, in seconds.

knobs.name: Rush Harmony Interval /s
knobs.description: Rush Audio: seconds between harmonic chord changes (2-4s).
knobs.docstring: Seconds between harmonic chord changes during sustained rush mode (2-4s).

knobs.name: Audio Presence Window Ms
knobs.description: How long after a player action the game still counts them as PRESENT. Phase 2's idle music fade is what will consume this; nothing reads it today (see Audio.player_is_present).
knobs.docstring: How long after a player action the game still counts them as PRESENT. Phase 2's idle music fade is what will consume this; nothing reads it today (see Audio.player_is_present).

knobs.name: Audio Scaled Min Db
knobs.description: How quiet the smallest version of an intensity-scaled sound is, relative to its loudest.
knobs.docstring: How quiet the smallest version of an intensity-scaled sound is, relative to its loudest.

knobs.name: Audio Layer Threshold
knobs.description: The intensity at which a scaled sound starts mixing in its brighter layer.
knobs.docstring: The intensity at which a scaled sound starts mixing in its brighter layer.

knobs.name: Audio Buy Intensity Min Fraction
knobs.description: The income/sec change (as a fraction) that a purchase must produce to reach the FLOOR and the CEILING of the purchase sound's intensity. A +2% buy sits at the floor, a +50% buy maxes out. Fractions, never dollars — the same purchase must sound the same at every generation.
